newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN rights body urges probe into Zaire massacres.
newsitem.headline: UN rights body urges probe into Zaire massacres.

text.p: The U.N. human rights body called on Tuesday for further investigation into reported massacres of Rwandan Hutu refugees in rebel-controlled eastern Zaire.

A resolution adopted by consensus at the 53-member U.N. Human Rights Commission also called on the Zaire government and rebels to stop fighting and negotiate a settlement to the crisis in the vast central African country.
U.N. human rights investigator for Zaire, Roberto Garreton, has accused the Tutsi-dominated rebels of massacring thousands of civilians and Rwandan Hutu refugees since December.

The resolution asked Garreton and the U.N. human rights investigator on extrajudicial, summary or arbitrary executions to investigate the massacres and report to the U.N. General Assembly in New York by June 30.

Garreton has called for a broad U.N. inquiry into the killings and urged U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan to provide his commission of inquiry with forensic and ballistic experts to excavate mass graves. U.N. human rights officials say he has yet to receive funding from new York for the job.
